statement_closure.notes: J is an R-submodule of C, QJ is its rational span, and the supplied N003 explicitly states finite generation, nonzeroness and dimension one. R, the finite index set, e, M_R and mu are defined; their needed guards are supplied by H001 and N001. The output quantifies one common nonzero b in J and states the internal sum and both bases. background_notes.fact: If L is a one-dimensional Q-subspace of C, 0 != a belongs to L, and a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of L is given, then J has a finite nonempty generating list q_1 a,...,q_k a with each q_j a nonzero and each q_j in Q\{0}.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated and dim_Q QJ=1.
QJ is the rational span of J, so J is contained in QJ.
a is chosen nonzero in J.

background_notes.justification: A nonzero vector in a one-dimensional vector space spans it: relative to any one-element basis, its coefficient is nonzero and can be inverted. Express each member of a finite generating list in this basis a. Removing zero members preserves the generated submodule and cannot remove all members since J is nonzero. The surviving rational coefficients are nonzero.

background_notes.fact: For a positive prime integer p and any nonzero rational q, there are nu in Z and u in Q with q=p^nu u and both u and u^(-1) in Z_(p). A finite nonempty list of such integer exponents has an attained minimum.

grounds.reason: F001 gives finitely many nonzero rational coefficients with positive list length.
R consists of rational fractions whose denominator is not divisible by p.

background_notes.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. For each nonzero integer m, the exponents e>=0 for which p^e divides m form a nonempty finite set: divisibility implies p^e<=|m| and p>=2 bounds e. Choose its largest exponent. Thus A=p^alpha A' and B=p^beta B', with neither A' nor B' divisible by p. Set nu=alpha-beta and u=A'/B'. Both u and its reciprocal have allowed denominators in R, so u is an R-unit. Negative nu causes no problem in Q. Comparing finitely many integer entries recursively yields an entry realizing their minimum. This is the factorization and minimum construction already used in S002.

background_notes.fact: If R is a subring of C, (e_i) is a finite C-linearly independent family, b is a nonzero complex scalar and L is the internal sum of R(b e_i), then (b e_i) is an R-basis of L. If mu:T->V is R-linear, injective and has image L, the unique preimages of this family form an R-basis of T.

grounds.reason: R is viewed as a subring of C.
The e_i form a complex basis.
mu is R-linear with the stated image notation.
The image of mu is the internal sum of J e_i.
F003 gives b nonzero and J=Rb.

background_notes.justification: In a finite relation sum_i r_i b e_i=0, complex independence gives r_i b=0 for every i. Since b is nonzero, every r_i=0 in C and hence in R. The displayed sum supplies spanning. Each vector in this basis lies in the image of mu, so has a unique preimage. Applying mu proves independence of the preimages; expressing mu(t) in the image basis and using injectivity proves their spanning.
